mcpPage.label: MCP server
mcpPage.addDescription: Connect a local command or a remote server so runs can use its tools, resources, and prompts.
mcpPage.connectionDescription: The server’s name, and how the app starts it on this computer or reaches it over the network.
mcpPage.authDescription: How the app signs in to the server.
mcpPage.authCodeNote: Finish signing in with your browser. If it shows an authorization code, paste it in this server's row in the list.
mcpPage.serverIdHint: Letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores. The ID can't be changed after the server is added.
mcpPage.transportStdioHint: Starts the command on this computer and talks to it over standard input and output.
mcpPage.transportHttpHint: Connects to a remote server at the URL over Streamable HTTP.
mcpPage.transportSseHint: Connects to an older remote server that streams over Server-Sent Events.
mcpPage.argumentsHint: One argument per line. Spaces stay part of the argument, so no quoting is needed.
mcpPage.tokenEnvHint: The service reads the token from this environment variable when it connects. If the variable is unset, it uses the token saved in the system credential store.
mcpPage.oauthHint: After saving, choose Authenticate to sign in with your browser.
mcpPage.unkeptNote: This page can't edit these settings. Saving keeps them, except when you switch between a command and a URL transport, which drops the ones that no longer apply.
mcpPage.authNoneHint: If the server asks you to sign in, choose Authenticate in its status.
mcpPage.oauthSectionNote: All optional. Fill these in when the server needs a client registered in advance or points to the wrong authorization server. Left empty, the app registers a client itself.
mcpPage.clientNameHint: The name the app registers its own client under. Leave empty to use the app's name.
mcpPage.clientSecretHint: Kept in the system credential store and sent only to this client's authorization server. It needs a client ID.
mcpPage.clientSecretReplacePlaceholder: New secret, or empty to remove it
mcpPage.callbackPortHint: The local port in the redirect URI the client was registered with. Leave empty to use any free port.
mcpPage.metadataUrlHint: Where sign-in finds the authorization server instead of asking the MCP server. Codes, tokens, and the client secret go where it says, so it must use https:// (http:// only on localhost).
mcpPage.accessDescription: How the agent reaches the server’s tools and resources.
mcpPage.exposureAutoHint: Tools are always available when the server has up to {{threshold}}; with more, the agent searches for them when it needs them.
mcpPage.exposureAutoNowDirect_one: This server lists {{count}} tool, no more than {{threshold}}, so it's always available.
mcpPage.exposureAutoNowDirect_other: This server lists {{count}} tools, no more than {{threshold}}, so they're always available.
mcpPage.exposureAutoNowDeferred_one: This server lists {{count}} tool, more than {{threshold}}, so the agent searches for it when it needs it.
mcpPage.exposureAutoNowDeferred_other: This server lists {{count}} tools, more than {{threshold}}, so the agent searches for them when it needs them.
mcpPage.exposureDirectHint: Every tool is offered to the agent with each request. Best for servers with a few tools.
mcpPage.exposureDeferredHint: Tools stay out of each request until the agent searches for them, which saves context on servers with many tools.
mcpPage.resourcesHint: The agent can list and read the files and data this server shares as resources.
mcpPage.pluginAccessNote: Plugin servers load tools automatically and don't share resources with the agent. To change this, duplicate the server to Personal.

computer.title: Computer use
computer.description: Atd requests access to the apps and websites a task needs. Automatic and Full approval save approved access here for later tasks; Manual approval lasts for one run. Remove a target here to revoke its saved access. Automations use only their separately authorized scope.

ready.title: Ready
ready.description: Atd can act on your targets in the background. In tasks you run, when the background can’t do a step in an app, Atd briefly brings the app forward and sends that step’s clicks and keys straight to it, without moving your pointer, then switches back to the app you were using.

starting.title: Starting…

unavailable.title: Unavailable

unsettled.title: Background computer use is paused
unsettled.description_one: Atd couldn’t confirm whether {{count}} action changed anything. Until you check the apps and websites your computer automations use, they won’t act on them in the background.
unsettled.description_other: Atd couldn’t confirm whether {{count}} actions changed anything. Until you check the apps and websites your computer automations use, they won’t act on them in the background.
unsettled.confirmDescription: Confirm that you looked at the apps and websites these actions may have changed and fixed anything that wasn’t right. Atd records them as done with an unknown result and won’t repeat them.

supportDiagnostics.description: Reproduce the issue, then export the log and send it to support. Saving the ZIP stops recording and clears the internal diagnostic cache.
supportDiagnostics.stoppedDescription: Start a fresh recording when you need to reproduce another issue. Your exported ZIP files are kept.
supportDiagnostics.privacy: Includes app versions, runtime states, request outcomes and timing. No chat content, typed text, request bodies or screenshots. The report is saved locally.
supportDiagnostics.startFailed: Diagnostic recording could not be started. Try again.
supportDiagnostics.saved: Diagnostic ZIP saved. Recording has stopped and the internal cache is cleared. Send the ZIP file to support.
supportDiagnostics.cleanupFailed: The diagnostic ZIP was saved and is valid. Recording has stopped for now, but internal cache or saved-state cleanup failed. Recording may resume when you reopen this build. Send the ZIP file to support.
supportDiagnostics.cancelled: Export cancelled. Recording continues and the diagnostic log is kept.
supportDiagnostics.failed: The diagnostic log could not be saved. Try again and choose a writable folder.
supportDiagnostics.permissionHint: Allow Accessibility in System Settings. If prompted, also allow Input Monitoring. Reopen this build if macOS requests it; then close System Settings and reproduce the issue. You can still export a partial log.
supportDiagnostics.permissionFailed: Could not open System Settings. Open Privacy & Security to allow Accessibility and any requested Input Monitoring.
supportDiagnostics.focusTitle: Runtime and window focus recording is on
supportDiagnostics.focusPrivacy: Includes runtime states, request outcomes, app identities, mouse clicks, window states and permissions. No chat content, typed text, request bodies or screenshots. The report is saved locally.
